I work on the genetics of disease resistance in lettuce — in particular how the crop
responds to necrotrophic fungal pathogens, and how that response can be read at the
level of individual transcripts rather than whole genes.

My current work combines time-series transcriptomics, reference transcriptome
construction and CRISPR-Cas9 genome editing to identify and test candidate regulators
of resistance. Before moving into plant pathology and molecular biology, I worked in
seed science on the longevity, storage and priming of vegetable seed.

## Research interests

- Plant immunity and resistance to necrotrophic fungal pathogens
- Transcript-level expression analysis and alternative splicing
- Reference transcriptome construction
- CRISPR-Cas9 genome editing in crops
- Seed longevity, storage and priming
